aspect: The asymmetry is structural, not accidental
description: Inbound remittance is a foreign-exchange source and is facilitated. Outbound payment and inbound business revenue are controlled, because both touch scarce hard currency.
energy_note: Easy to be sent money. Hard to earn it.

aspect: Multiple exchange rates mean the official one costs you
description: Where official and parallel rates diverge, receiving through formal channels converts at the worse rate, so the compliant route is the expensive one.
money_note: Annual loss to the rate differential.
energy_note: Punished, in percentage terms, for using the legal route.

description: She sends her mother money monthly from Manchester. The transfer fee is modest, the rate is not, and the difference across a year is roughly what her mother's medication costs. She has never mentioned this to her mother.
energy_note: A year of the exchange rate, priced in tablets.

description: Her son's fees in Accra are USD 2,400 a term. Sending it through the bank converts at the official rate and requires documentation of purpose; sending it the other way is faster, cheaper and technically an offence. She has done both and only tells her husband about one of them.
energy_note: The legal route, and the one that works.
